title: Shoggoth wall art — round 13: H refined and aired out
notes: Air it out inside 3x3 ft with a smaller body (H13), or go ~4 ft wide with the body at full size (E1)? And do the grown shelves + umber finish work? Sketches welcome, never waited on. ··· WHAT CHANGED vs round 12 (all your likes applied, nothing re-opened): ball B1; one umber finish with only the ball and teeth bone-pale (K1); shelves grown out of the limbs, each one different (K4); the whip now forks off a limb instead of a shelf; the eye patch blends into the trunk; the root cascade starts staggered. Eye groups unchanged (K2). AIR (K3): H13 stays 914 mm wide by shrinking the body group to 84%; the gap from each shelf to the body grows from 52-80 mm to 99-104 mm. E1 keeps the body at full size and stretches the arms: 1206 x 842 mm, gaps 214-250 mm. The plant views use rough stand-in plants (one upright, two trailing). STRUCTURAL (shelf arms, checked this round for the first time against the shelf-arm rule; my miss that rounds 7-12 were not): the thin upper-left arm, including round 11's, cannot hold a plant as a plain print. Fix that keeps it exactly as drawn: a pre-bent 12 mm steel rod inside. With it, H13 carries a full 5 kg plant; E1 carries ~2.5 kg (a trailing plant), or 5 kg with one buttress tentacle under the shelf. The other two arms: H13 needs one solid-printed arm; E1 needs 16 mm steel rods in both (35-38% more load at the wall). Both need 2 screws per row into each stud; E1 spans 3 studs. STUD MAP still needed from you. Composition gate (information only): H13 3/7 (the smaller body drops out of the torso/fill bands), E1 4/7; round-11 H was 6/7. FLUX concept art: one last free-quota try tomorrow. Not yet peer-signed: CAD r13 README, Structural shelf-arms-r13.

cards.title: H13 — H refined, inside 3x3 ft (front + three-quarter)
cards.rationale: Your round-12 likes applied to H: ball B1, umber finish, shelves grown from the limbs (lobed, thin rims, ribs flowing from the limb), whip forking off a limb, eye patch blended, staggered cascade. Arms longer by shrinking the body group to 84%; shelves at the 914 mm edges.

cards.title: H13 with stand-in plants
cards.rationale: Mix as you suggested: trailing vines on the two left shelves, an upright plant on the right. Rough proxies at assumed sizes, muted pots. Does the creature still read with plants on it?

cards.title: E1 — same, but ~4 ft wide (1206 x 842 mm)
cards.rationale: Everything as H13, but the body stays full size and the arms reach out: shelf-to-body gaps 214-250 mm (vs 99-104 in H13). Cost: steel rods in all three shelf arms, the upper-left shelf limited to ~2.5 kg (or a buttress tentacle), 3 studs, more print segments.

cards.title: E1 with stand-in plants
cards.rationale: Same plant mix as H13's card. The wider spread leaves the body clear of the vines.

cards.title: Side views — H13 (left), E1 (right)
cards.rationale: The ball held off the eye patch, and the grown shelf plates from the side (round 12's K4 question showed plates on stalks).
